extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers, state and federal regulators, policy analysts, and stakeholders commenting on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and evaluate regulatory criteria and metrics the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) uses to justify proposing to discontinue standardized plan options and non-standardized plan option limits for QHPs on FFEs and SBE-FPs. Covers enrollment metrics, consumer behavior evidence, regulatory burdens, plan design features, and exceptions processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uptake of standardized plan options (enrollment share)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of total enrollment in standardized plan options (e.g., "only 20 percent of total enrollment in the FFEs and SBE-FPs was in standardized plan options in PY 2023, 33 percent in PY 2024, and 33 percent in PY 2025").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate whether standardized options appeal to consumers; low uptake suggests plans fail to appeal or consumers cannot perceive meaningful difference between standardized and non-standardized plan options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of plan offerings that are standardized plan options
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of total plan offerings that are standardized (e.g., "25 percent of total plan offerings were standardized plan options in PY 2023, 28 percent in PY 2024, and 31 percent in PY 2025").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compares availability of standardized plans vs enrollment to assess mismatch between offerings and consumer take-up; used to assess whether increased offerings translate to consumer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active plan selections (consumer-initiated choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of consumers who actively selected standardized plan options (excludes auto-reenrollment), e.g., "only 18 percent of consumers in the FFEs and SBE-FPs actively selected standardized plan options in PY 2023, 26 percent in PY 2024, and 18 percent in PY 2025."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower-than-expected active selection rates are interpreted as evidence standardized plans fail to appeal or are not meaningfully distinguishable to consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of differential display on HealthCare.gov and DE pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and form of differential display features (labeling as 'easy pricing', icons, hover text, 'quick tip', and filter to view only standardized plans) that visually distinguish standardized plans from non-standardized plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite a "full suite of differential display features" that explain benefits and distinctive features, non-standardized plans remained more popular; therefore, differential display alone may be insufficient to increase uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of non-standardized plan option limits on availability and consumer choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on the number of non-standardized plan options (four in PY 2024, reduced to two in PY 2025) and the degree to which these limits reduce plan proliferation and influence enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated by comparing weighted averages of plans per enrollee and plans per issuer before and after limits; marginal net reductions observed do not appear to justify the burdens imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan proliferation metrics (weighted averages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary metric: "the weighted average number of total QHPs available per enrollee in the FFEs and SBE-FPs" and related metric: "the weighted average number of total plans offered per issuer." Examples: 108 plans/enrollee (PY2022) → 114 (PY2023) → 100 (PY2024–PY2025); plans per issuer 16.9 → 17.3 → 14.7 → 13.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify plan proliferation and to judge whether policy interventions meaningfully reduced choice overload; HHS considers marginal reductions insufficient evidence of success given burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice overload evidence and literature benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical research cited about number of choices and enrollment outcomes (e.g., RAND review and studies of Medicare programs showing a choice of 15 or fewer plans associated with higher enrollment, while 30+ plans led to declines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides theoretical/empirical justification for limiting choices; used to weigh potential consumer decision-making benefits against regulatory burdens and market effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on issuers and HHS from requiring standardized plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and operational costs including creating new plans that conform to HHS-specified designs, submitting additional certification applications for standardized plans and exception-process plans, and adjusting issuers' plan portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS treats increased fixed costs, certification burden, and market inefficiencies (including plan discontinuations and consumer disruption) as negative outcomes weighed against benefits of standardization and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer experience objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Original policy goals: "enhancing the consumer experience, increasing consumer understanding, and simplifying the decision-making process for consumers purchasing coverage through the Exchanges."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS assesses whether standardized plan options and limits actually improved these outcomes; finding they have failed to achieve these objectives is a key basis for proposing removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to combat discriminatory benefit designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether standardized plan designs (e.g., exempting primary care, specialist visits, mental health/substance use outpatient office visits, therapies, and generic drugs from the deductible; requiring flat copayments vs coinsurance) reduce discriminatory benefit designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS notes these design features were chosen to reduce barriers to access and promote certainty but also observes such features are common in non-standardized plans, so standardization may not be necessary to achieve anti-discrimination goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized plan design methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Design approach used for standardized options: select the most popular cost sharing type for each benefit category; select enrollee-weighted median cost sharing values (and for annual limitation on cost sharing and deductible) based on refreshed data; modify to accommodate State laws; decrease AVs to floor of each AV de minimis range (primarily by increasing deductibles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how HHS constructs standardized options to mirror market consensus; used to judge how distinct standardized plans are from market offerings and whether they meaningfully differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions process criteria for chronic and high-cost condition plans
rubrics_metrics.description: For PY2025 exceptions, issuers could offer additional non-standardized plans if they "demonstrate that these additional non-standardized plans have specific design features that would substantially benefit consumers with chronic and high-cost conditions" by showing cost sharing for treatment would be reduced by 25% or more relative to the issuer's other non-standardized offerings in the same product/metal/service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A quantitative threshold (25% reduction) used to judge eligibility for exceptions intended to preserve targeted plans for medically complex populations while limiting plan proliferation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for discontinuing or modifying plans (crosswalks, plan ID, auto-reenrollment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If issuers discontinue standardized or exceptions-process plans, enrollees will be crosswalked per the crosswalk hierarchy at §155.335(j); if issuers continue same-cost-sharing standardized plans, enrollees are auto-reenrolled; substantial modifications typically create a new plan ID and trigger crosswalking unless State rules or uniform modification exceptions (e.g., §147.106(e)(3)(iv)) allow retention of same plan ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes operational and consumer-protection rules that would govern transitions, and the potential for minimizing disruption if modifications meet uniform modification criteria tied to changes in cost/utilization or maintaining metal tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on issuer flexibility and plan innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardization and non-standardized limits constrained ability to offer plan features such as tiered provider networks, separate medical and drug deductibles or MOOPs, HSA-eligible HDHPs, and plans with more than four tiers of prescription drug coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS views removal of requirements as restoring flexibility for issuer innovation and expanding consumer choice in plan features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net benefit vs regulatory complexity and market disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall assessment weighing modest/marginal reductions in plan proliferation metrics against increased regulatory complexity, administrative burden, fixed costs for issuers, market disruption, and significant plan discontinuations and affected enrollees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS concludes marginal improvements do not outweigh disadvantages; forms core rationale for proposing to remove the suite of policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing standardized and non-standardized plans as an added decision variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that offering standardized plans alongside non-standardized plans "served as yet another variable that consumers must consider during the plan selection process," potentially undermining the goal of reducing cognitive load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to question whether partial standardization (coexisting with non-standardized options) accomplishes simplification objectives and to motivate consideration of alternative or narrower interventions (e.g., requiring standardization only at selected metal levels or service areas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory alternatives solicitation (targeted standardization options)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS seeks comment on alternatives such as requiring standardized plan options only at particular metal levels (e.g., bronze and silver) or only in certain service areas where issuers offer a certain number of non-standardized options, or reverting to voluntary standardized offerings while maintaining differential display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates HHS is evaluating narrower policy designs as potential less-burdensome ways to achieve objectives; solicits stakeholder input on feasibility and likely impacts.
